name: The Raincoats
label: Rough Trade
lede: Two art students saw the Slits, picked up instruments they barely knew how to play, and made a record so unlike anything around it that Kurt Cobain traipsed across London looking for a copy thirteen years later.

hero.by: The Raincoats at MoMA, New York, November 2010. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Permission from the Slits
eras.text: Gina Birch came from Nottingham to study at Hornsey College of Art and barely knew how to play bass. She and Ana da Silva watched The Slits and decided that was enough of a qualification.

q: It was as if suddenly I was given permission.
years.src: Wikipedia: The Raincoats · The Guardian: Gina Birch
years.h: Birch and da Silva see the Slits and start a band
years.p: Two Hornsey College of Art students decide girls can do this too.

years.h: First gig at the Tabernacle, with two men in the band
years.p: Birch and da Silva play with Ross Crighton on guitar and Nick Turner on drums. Turner leaves to form The Barracudas.

years.h: A drummer from the 101ers and a guitarist who makes films
years.p: Kate Korus of the Slits passes through, then Jeremie Frank. [[Richard Dudanski|9304c467-0450-4c16-b7d1-118cd8f7a2c5]], once of the The 101ers, sits in on drums, and future filmmaker Patrick Keiller plays guitar.

years.cap: The Raincoats at the Crypt, Paddington, September 22, 1978
years.src: Wikipedia: The Raincoats · The Guardian: Gina Birch
years.h: Palmolive and a classical violinist make it all-female
years.p: Ex-Slits drummer [[Palmolive|e714dc21-11e0-4205-b114-f3b3018c2c74]] and classically trained violinist [[Vicky Aspinall|1fc07353-4be1-4460-8329-44d4bb6a43c7]] join. Aspinall also introduces Birch to feminism.

eras.title: Lola, a violin and a supermarket
eras.text: Rough Trade's Geoff Travis brought in Mayo Thompson of Red Krayola to produce, and the band found a sound with a violin pointed at the Velvet Underground. Some critics hated it. A good many musicians who would matter later took notes.

years.h: The new line-up debuts at Acklam Hall
years.p: Birch, da Silva, Aspinall and Palmolive play Acklam Hall in London. NME's Ian Penman reviews the show.

years.h: 'Fairytale in the Supermarket' is the first single
years.p: Thompson and Travis suggest Aspinall play violin the way John Cale played viola in the [[The Velvet Underground|94b0fb9d-a066-4823-b2ec-af1d324bcfcf]].

years.h: The first UK tour, with Swiss band Kleenex
years.p: Manager Shirley O'Loughlin takes them out with Kleenex, later [[LiLiPUT|83bae41e-e95e-4540-8dfa-2254563858dc]]. Reactions split hard.
years.xp:
Johnny Rotten became an admirer, and later said women like the Raincoats were involved in punk "for no other reason than that they were good and original".

Danny Baker, after an early show, said they were so bad that every time a waiter dropped a tray everyone got up to dance.

years.h: Palmolive leaves just before the album; Ingrid Weiss takes over
years.p: The teenage drummer joins weeks before the debut album comes out.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Raincoats (album) · Wikipedia: The Raincoats
years.h: The Raincoats, with a cover of the Kinks' 'Lola'
years.p: Recorded at Berry Street Studio in Clerkenwell with Thompson and Travis, catalogue ROUGH 3. It reaches No. 5 on the indie chart.
years.xp:
Birch on Thompson: "He gave me confidence to use my instinct to make something, forging something out of nothing."

It took decades for the wider world to catch up. Rolling Stone put it at No. 398 on its 2020 list of the 500 greatest albums, and Jenn Pelly wrote a 33⅓ book on it in 2017.

years.h: Junk-shop instruments come home from New York
years.p: From markets, second-hand shops and a 1980 trip to New York, the band collects a shruti box, balophone, kalimba, shehnai and finger cymbals. They're all on the next album.

eras.title: Odyshape and the slow drift
eras.text: With a rotating cast of drummers, including Robert Wyatt, the Raincoats made a second album that sounded even less like rock music, which was the point. Three albums in, they drifted into other projects.

years.h: Robert Wyatt and Charles Hayward drum on Odyshape
years.p: Weiss leaves during the sessions; Wyatt, This Heat's Charles Hayward and Dudanski fill in. Produced by Adam Kidron at Berry Street, it reaches No. 5 on the indie chart.
years.xp:
Speaking to Greil Marcus, the band said rock and roll was built on the exclusion of women, "which is why we want to put a bit of distance between what we do and the rock'n'roll tradition."

Pitchfork later said the album had "little in common with anything else around at the time". Kim Gordon wrote its reissue liner notes.

years.h: A live set at the Kitchen in New York becomes a cassette
years.p: Recorded at the downtown arts space, The Kitchen Tapes comes out on ROIR in 1983.

years.h: Moving is the last album for twelve years
years.p: Tired of touring and pulling in different directions, they move to solo work. Birch and Aspinall form Dorothy; da Silva works with choreographer Gaby Agis and starts Roseland with Charles Hayward.

eras.title: Kurt Cobain goes looking
eras.text: Nirvana's singer went shopping for a used record in west London and ended up giving the band a second life. He died before he could take them on tour.

years.big: "It made me happier than playing in front of thousands of people"
years.h: Cobain goes hunting for a Raincoats LP in London
years.p: Cobain in the Incesticide liner notes. Rough Trade's shop on Talbot Road sent him round the corner to da Silva at her cousin's antique shop; she later mailed him the first album.
years.xp:
He wrote that the record reminded him of a time when he was "extremely unhappy, lonely, and bored", and that listening to it felt like being a stowaway in their attic.

Cobain later put The Raincoats at No. 21 in his list of 50 favourite albums.

years.h: DGC reissues all three albums with notes by Cobain and Kim Gordon
years.p: Rough Trade and Nirvana's label put The Raincoats, Odyshape and Moving back in shops. Gordon wrote that they seemed like ordinary people playing extraordinary music.

years.cap: The Raincoats with Liz Phair at the Academy, New York, 1994
years.h: Steve Shelley drums at the Garage; a Nirvana tour is next
years.p: O'Loughlin talks Birch and da Silva into a reunion show with [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]]'s [[Steve Shelley|998815d5-03bc-4228-807f-b550c07038d2]] and violinist Anne Wood. Cobain invites them on Nirvana's April UK tour. He dies a week before it starts.
years.xp:
A John Peel session from that spring came out as Extended Play on Blast First and Shelley's Smells Like Records.

Da Silva later said they hadn't thought about another record: "We weren't really a band at the time."

years.h: John Cale gives them 20 minutes in a Paris café, and they pass
years.p: Ed Buller produces Looking in the Shadows for Rough Trade and Geffen instead, at Trident, with ex-Tiger Trap drummer Heather Dunn and Pete Shelley guesting.
years.xp:
Bikini Kill's Tobi Vail turned the drum job down; she was, she said, a four-four drummer and their songs weren't. Dunn, 21, auditioned in London and got it.

Cale had agreed to produce for $20,000 but would only work in New York and on his schedule. "He didn't want to do it, so we didn't want to do it," Birch said.

eras.title: Grandmothers of riot grrrl, still playing
eras.text: Reissued on their own label, invited to festivals by the musicians they'd influenced, the Raincoats kept playing in their own time while Birch painted and made a solo record.

years.cap: The Raincoats at MoMA, New York, November 2010
years.h: The Raincoats play the Museum of Modern Art
years.p: A PopRally show in New York, months after they played the debut album in full at London's Scala for ATP's Don't Look Back series.

years.h: Birch, 67, releases her first solo album on Third Man
years.p: I Play My Bass Loud, made with producer Youth, includes a dub song about never wearing stilettos. You couldn't run from Teddy boys in them, she says.

years.h: Shouting Out Loud, the first full biography, is published
years.p: Audrey Golden's book covers the band from Hornsey to the DGC years, including the drummer hunt and the Cale meeting.
